projects.name: Cross-Carrier Wave
projects.I: Provenance-preserving carrier/transform experiments across representations and domains.
projects.R: Faithful compression/translation/abstraction must remain distinct from concealed consequential loss.
projects.P: Use adaptive typed carriers, explicit transform states, one-degree probes, and carried loss/remainder.
projects.O: Adaptive carrier overlays and explicit loss accounting were retained; universal-theory interpretations were rejected.
projects.highlight: Transform contracts now carry provenance, change, loss, uncertainty, ethics/cost, and remainder.
projects.lowlight: Early fixed-dimensional and universal-coordinate readings exceeded the evidence.
projects.claimCeiling: Research architecture; not a completed theory of knowledge or universal semantic geometry.

checks.assumption: Consequential distinctions can be identified locally enough to test preservation.
checks.test: Ablate or alter one carrier/transform relation and test reconstructibility.
checks.unknown: Broad real-world benefit outside bounded experiments remains unestablished.

projects.name: Orbit Library
projects.I: A compact active navigation surface with recoverable source/history/support layers.
projects.R: Useful navigation is not exhaustive historical identity or evidence authority.
projects.P: Prefer source-native reconstruction, exact identity, cold locators when earned, and explicit unknown/unassigned states.
projects.O: Compact navigation works, but root-edge audits proved exact file-level historical coverage remains partial.
projects.highlight: Current/history/support and exact-source boundaries became explicit.
projects.lowlight: Later historical catalogs omitted genuine predecessor identities.
projects.claimCeiling: Navigation/recovery infrastructure; not a complete model of the Library.

checks.assumption: A small active surface is preferable when exact recovery remains possible.
checks.test: Freeze loose-root samples and measure exact recovery, family representation, ambiguity, and unresolved cases.
checks.unknown: The benefit/cost threshold for broader exact-file indexing remains unresolved.

projects.name: Tiny Babel / TBCL
projects.I: Finite language/retrieval/reorganization research plus later TBCL runtime/reconstruction work.
projects.R: Subject/obligation must remain distinct from carrier/index/hierarchy/runtime representation.
projects.P: Preserve the finite subject, exact verification boundary, strict semantics, and source/reconstruction separation.
projects.O: Finite exhaustive verification and carrier reduction succeeded within bounded inherited domains.
projects.highlight: Exhaustive finite verification replaced example-only confidence.
projects.lowlight: Finite success does not imply universal language, retrieval, or global minimality.

checks.assumption: The finite subject/query space faithfully represents the bounded claim.
checks.test: Exhaustive enumeration plus behavior comparison across carriers and independent verification where possible.
checks.unknown: Scaling to open-ended/noisy/culturally variable domains remains unresolved.

projects.name: Operator Moonshot
projects.I: Bounded mathematical, computational, educational, operator, and calibration experiments.
projects.R: Interesting mechanism, replicated result, general scientific claim, and open-problem solution are different evidence levels.
projects.P: Replicate before promotion, preserve failed replications, use calibration only as calibration, and attack with counterexamples/ablations.
projects.O: Evidence discipline strengthened; Cycle 3 replication and Education E3 robustness failures remain preserved.
projects.highlight: Causal ablation, replication, provenance, and claim ceilings became core practice.
projects.lowlight: Several promising branches failed replication/robustness and some original source remains missing.
projects.claimCeiling: Research laboratory/evidence ledger; not proof that larger open targets are solved.

checks.assumption: The experiment target, baseline, and evidence carrier actually measure the claimed relation.
checks.test: Replication, ablation, adversarial counterexamples, independent verification, and simpler baselines.
checks.unknown: Generalization outside finite/synthetic domains remains unresolved.

projects.name: Model Experiments
projects.I: PulseNet, PulseNet GP, SPDM, streaming/recurrent memory, Micro-Ouro, compressed-domain and related model experiments.
projects.R: Mechanism activity, usefulness, and causality must be tested separately.
projects.P: Keep runnable baselines, ablate proposed mechanisms, compare against trivial alternatives, and preserve regressions.
projects.O: Reusable machinery and negative evidence accumulated; several mechanisms changed outputs without earning usefulness claims.
projects.highlight: Model work increasingly separated execution correctness, numerical stability, and predictive usefulness.
projects.lowlight: Regressions, baseline errors, weak reasoning cores, and below-chance checkpoints were found and retained.
projects.claimCeiling: Bounded implementation/experiment evidence; no general intelligence or universal reasoning claim.

checks.assumption: Benchmarks distinguish proposed mechanisms from simpler alternatives.
checks.test: Frozen data/baselines, ablation, multi-seed reruns, held-out performance, and stability checks.
checks.unknown: Value after training, scaling, native implementation, domain shift, and stronger baselines remains unresolved.

projects.name: Geometry, 4D Codecs, and Observer Experiments
projects.I: 3D/4D geometry, topology, inversion, compact encodings, finite observer/classification, and float64 carrier experiments.
projects.R: Useful/correct representation is not evidence of physical truth.
projects.P: Test round trips, corruption, inverse transforms, finite confounds, and raw-bit/numeric boundaries independently.
projects.O: Engineering mechanisms survived; over-strong physical interpretations and rigid fixed-dimensional stories were rejected.
projects.highlight: Encoding correctness and observer distinguishability became independently testable.
projects.lowlight: Geometric resemblance and finite discrimination can invite interpretations beyond the evidence.
projects.claimCeiling: Engineering and bounded mathematical experiments; no new physical theory claim.

checks.assumption: Encoding/transform specifications are explicit enough for independent testing.
checks.test: Exact encode/decode, perturbation, inverse-transform, confound enumeration, ablation, and integrity checks.
checks.unknown: Which representations correspond to deeper physical structure, if any, remains unresolved.

projects.name: Historical Recovery
projects.I: Old code, generic pasted sources, archives, later summaries, incomplete indexes, and source-native recovery evidence.
projects.R: Not found by an index is not absence; semantic resemblance is not project identity.
projects.P: Follow exact file IDs, chronology, archive membership, namespaces, migrations, and source hashes before assigning identity.
projects.O: Hidden predecessor identities were recovered; Fuzzball remains an explicit unresolved carrier and a prior black-hole conflation was corrected.
projects.highlight: FractalDeflectiveEngine and GrandUnifiedPerceptron predecessor identities were recovered from obscured carriers.
projects.lowlight: Fuzzball and the original structured solver/operator-lab source remain unresolved gaps; some archive bytes are inaccessible.
projects.claimCeiling: Recovery graph only; missing carriers remain unresolved rather than substituted.

checks.assumption: User-attested historical projects are legitimate recovery targets without implying a relation to candidate files.
checks.test: Exact source, namespace, archive path, hash, chronology, and independent migration/provenance references.
checks.unknown: The exact Fuzzball carrier, chronology, and relation to neighboring projects remain unresolved.

lessonPolicy.author: GPT-6 Astra Pro
lessonPolicy.contribution: Assistant-curated summaries; companion performs deterministic navigation, not independent scientific review.
lessonPolicy.scope: Selected non-personal technical lessons and general design constraints. Private archives and personal records are not published.
lessonPolicy.evidenceRule: Source-reported tests stay source-reported. API regression checks do not revalidate all underlying research.

lessons.title: Corrected continuation: 6,048 is not 12,096
lessons.statement: Current answers, all future protected answers, and exact updating of selected internal labels are distinct guarantees.
lessons.assumptions: Three states, two deterministic actions, binary output and binary carrier; 46,656 combinations.
lessons.evidence: The corrected report records 6,048 current-safe/future-output failures, plus 6,048 future-output-safe cases that fail the chosen-label update rule. Their sum 12,096 counts current-safe label noncongruence.
lessons.claimCeiling: Congruence plus current safety is sufficient, not necessary, for future-output preservation. Both v6 branches and the superseded interpretation remain traceable.

lessons.title: Choose the missing distinction, not the largest data volume
lessons.statement: Diagnosis can stop when one action is acceptable in every remaining world; exact world identification is not always required.
lessons.assumptions: Finite supplied worlds, acceptable-action sets, authorized passive queries, path budgets and worst-case query cost.
lessons.evidence: 8,192 configurations: 4,916 solvable and 3,276 unresolved; zero cost/status disagreements with a separate same-author enumerator; 19,664 solved world-path replays.
lessons.claimCeiling: Whole-cell intersection, not pairwise overlap. Model acceptability is not independently established real-world safety, consent or complete world coverage.

lessons.title: A missing source must not broaden an evidence query
lessons.statement: An omitted endpoint filter and a supplied but unresolved endpoint are different states.
lessons.assumptions: Conscience64 1.2.0 at the pinned predecessor commit; an explicit nonexistent from/to identifier.
lessons.evidence: The claim hunt and this update baseline both found get(missing)=null while search.advanced({from:missing}) returned all 508 graph relations.
lessons.claimCeiling: The successor must throw UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE; malformed supplied identifiers throw INVALID_REFERENCE. A rejected query is not a measured zero.

lessons.title: Bind de Bruijn addresses to the actual codebook
lessons.statement: Serialize the oriented codebook, its word address, and an unfinished construction as separate objects.
lessons.assumptions: Ordered exact tokens; fixed order, cycle, origin and direction; cyclic windows; explicit resource bounds.
lessons.evidence: DBS1, DBA1 and DBW1 distinguish cycle, digest-bound address and replayable walk. Rotation rebases position by (p-r) mod L. A stuck append-only walk is not proof that no cycle exists.
lessons.claimCeiling: The original education serializer was not recovered. This is a separate candidate, not a legacy migration, scalable implicit rank/unrank implementation or demonstrated learning outcome.

lessons.title: Two exact UTF-8 carriers, two different capacity contracts
lessons.statement: Six-byte integer chunks stored numerically as binary64 and ranked zero-to-eight-byte strings stored by raw bit mapping are different codecs.
lessons.assumptions: Strict UTF-8, agreed codec/version, exact length and bit-preserving transport; no semantic interpretation of numerical distance.
lessons.evidence: The chunk codec expands full chunks by 8/6. The ranking report counts 168,570,276,329,617,409 strings of zero through eight bytes, needing 58 distinguishing bits; its mapping avoids integer-to-float rounding.
lessons.claimCeiling: Exactly nine-byte UTF-8 strings already exceed 2^64 possibilities. Neither codec stores an arbitrary library in one float or grants extra capacity to another interpretation.

lessons.title: A closure certificate covers arbitrary finite grammar depth
lessons.statement: For E ::= x | y | z | N E E, complete Boolean behavior on eight input rows yields exactly 256 classes.
lessons.assumptions: N is NAND; tree expressions, one-byte symbols, no shared gates, free constants or implicit operators.
lessons.evidence: All 65,536 ordered class compositions were checked; shortest witnesses attain recorded costs and satisfy every composition inequality. The largest minimum is 29 bytes; 34,491 literal expressions through 11 bytes were counterchecked.
lessons.claimCeiling: This is a grammar-specific behavior/minimum certificate, not a circuit DAG lower bound, cognitive idea model, or proof about unrestricted programs.

lessons.title: Exact symbolic repair without enumerating 2^64 tables
lessons.statement: For baseline b, protected mask P, required mask R and target t, conflict is (b XOR t) AND P AND R. Without conflict, the unique minimum changed-row repair is (b AND NOT R) OR (t AND R).
lessons.assumptions: Fixed width; complements masked to that width; pointwise constraints and unit Hamming cost per changed output row.
lessons.evidence: The solution set has 2^(width-popcount(P OR R)) members. Widths 1-4 were checked over 69,904 constraint systems and 1,082,400 candidate membership checks.
lessons.claimCeiling: The proof applies to this pointwise predicate, not arbitrary causal, linguistic or program-edit constraints; it resolves neither side of P versus NP.

lessons.title: A small exact graph certificate, with the cycle claim corrected
lessons.assumptions: The exact graph and two deleted edges in the pinned repository certificate.
lessons.evidence: Deleting two edges leaves a bipartite graph. Three odd cycles have empty common edge intersection, ruling out one-edge deletion. Enumeration checked 524,288 complement-reduced cuts and found optimum 28.
lessons.claimCeiling: The three cycles are not pairwise edge-disjoint. This is one graph, not a general short-certificate theorem; the older certificate size was not independently remeasured.

lessons.title: Use a same-label anchor, and specify the empty domain
lessons.statement: For nonempty D, an anchor in a smallest nonempty label class of size k gives at most k-1 possible nonzero XOR translations; verify each against all m labelled points.
lessons.assumptions: Explicit partial Boolean table over a declared n-bit ambient space; exact domain and label preservation.
lessons.evidence: The pair criterion 2*N_t=m, direct preservation and Walsh autocorrelation agree in the reported small exhaustive panel. The adapter agrees on 6,651 tables; the stored target returns {7}.
lessons.claimCeiling: Empty D is preserved by every translation and requires ambient n. The anchor bound m(k-1) does not establish a wall-time speedup or general asymptotic improvement. Multiple carriers of one statistic are not independent evidence.

lessons.title: Valid round trips are weaker than strict input admission
lessons.statement: Validate declared length, exact payload count, integer domain, finite values, canonical padding, UTF-8 and any expected digest before accepting a numeric text carrier.
lessons.assumptions: The six-byte chunk format and its declared metadata contract.
lessons.evidence: The source decoder accepted impossible/negative lengths and ignored padding mutations. A strict candidate adapter rejected the recorded malformed cases while preserving tested valid encoder outputs.
lessons.claimCeiling: These failures concern a stronger admission boundary, not the valid-input round-trip theorem. A colocated digest is not source authentication; missing NPY/NPZ reconstruction remains NOT_RUN.

lessons.title: Small survivors can still carry an expensive query
lessons.statement: Account separately for exactness, build, size, query, composition, verification and recovery.
lessons.assumptions: Task-local SAT boundary relations and separately defined circuit survivor sets.
lessons.evidence: The selector family replaces m^2 explicit clauses with 2m-1 shared binary gates, but arbitrary shared circuits can retain a Circuit-SAT query. Matching, forests and balanced incidence offer distinct restricted structural routes.
lessons.claimCeiling: No universal survivor compression or asymptotic lower bound follows. Reusing an interface does not transfer mathematical evidence between projects.

lessons.title: Carry uncertainty and evaluation status through the interface
lessons.statement: Keep unknown, partial, failed, measured-zero, evaluation-complete and promotion-approved states distinct.
lessons.assumptions: A declared task and downstream decisions that depend on those differences.
lessons.evidence: The daily collation separates 20 mathematical/model-relative consequences from eight engineering/human implications and keeps their assumptions, dependencies and counterprobes.
lessons.claimCeiling: Logging expected and actual values is not comparison. A completed negative evaluation need not qualify a release. Software checks do not establish human outcomes.

lessons.title: The person is not the recorded model
lessons.statement: People, recorded human models, research materials, active working sets and assisting systems remain distinct; preserve necessary meaning before reducing interface effort.
lessons.assumptions: Human-directed aims, explicit task boundaries and separate authorship; no inferred private traits.
lessons.evidence: The daily work distinguishes material availability, encounter, understanding, endorsement, learning and benefit instead of counting artifacts as knowledge acquired.
lessons.claimCeiling: This is general design guidance, not a complete or validated model of a person, a learner assessment, or empirical benefit evidence.

lessons.title: Preserve the correction path rather than defend a result
lessons.statement: Retain predecessor evidence and reopen the smallest consequential distinction when sources, goals, permissions or dependencies change.
lessons.assumptions: Recovery is lawful, justified and available; privacy minimization still applies.
lessons.evidence: The M01 correction, de Bruijn origin binding and unresolved-reference defect each identify a different relation that a compact representation must retain.
lessons.claimCeiling: Knowledge Decay is not only technical freshness. Recovering a record, restoring usable practice and showing human benefit require different evidence. No automatic cross-project authority transfer.
